question: Does the staged authorization, validation, publication, and post-flight design enforce the production repair security boundary strongly enough to replace the current workflow?
rationale: This PR intentionally replaces credential possession, artifact trust, source-state verification, and mutation ordering across production jobs; automated review can verify invariants but cannot accept that operational boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Approve after canary
options.body: Approve after all exact-head checks pass and one controlled repair demonstrates receipt-bound publication and fail-closed recovery.

options.title: Split the rollout
options.body: Land staged proof planning first while deferring the privileged publication topology to a separate, independently canaried change.

options.title: Pause the redesign
options.body: Retain the current workflow if maintainers do not want to own the added operational complexity and new failure modes.

recommendation.title: Approve after canary
recommendation.body: Approve after all exact-head checks pass and one controlled repair demonstrates receipt-bound publication and fail-closed recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history and this branch both place Vincent Koc at the center of the repair execution and post-flight behavior being redesigned.
